criteria.bundled_call: Provide one adapter entry per descriptor that performs upstream Parse then Scan internally and yields a unified compiler-owned value of statements, tokens, offsets, and failure. Parse output without its companion scan is unrepresentable.

criteria.separate_calls: Provide two adapter entries, Parse and Scan, each yielding its own compiler-owned value. I37 calls both once for every descriptor while retaining the freedom to test and reuse each pass independently.

fixed_constraints: P12 standardizes on libpg_query at one PostgreSQL major with the true parser and scanner in play: exactly one sanctioned statement per descriptor, unbroken $1..$N application parameters, scanner byte offsets that dice static SQL into Bun tagged-template slices, and a top-level LIMIT riding its own final parameter. Bespoke SQL lexing, parsing, or query logic is out; backend-shaped ASTs stay out of checker files; scanner shortfalls never license a fallback lexer.

Both contenders package PostgreSQL 17.7 (PG_VERSION_NUM 170007): pg_query_go/v6 v6.2.2 of 2026-01-28 carrying libpg_query 17-6.2.2, and go-pgquery v0.0.0-20260915022521-81f99195012b of 2026-09-15 carrying wazero v1.12.0 with a 2488452-byte in-binary WebAssembly module compiled from the same 17.7 tree. go-pgquery produces pg_query_go/v6 protobuf types.

Twenty-four probes (everyday/repeated/multi-digit parameters; single/escape/dollar-quoted strings; line and nested block comments; multibyte UTF-8 ahead of tokens; invalid grammar; unterminated strings; multi/empty/comment-only/semicolon-only bodies; INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, RETURNING-bearing or plain; subquery and literal LIMIT) yield identical raw parse and scan JSON, token extents, statement extents, parameter identities and extents, and failure text with cursor. Go error wrapper naming alone varies (*parser.Error versus *pgerror.Error).

Apple M4 darwin/arm64 numbers: cold parse+scan of the 105-byte P13 SELECT in a new process costs near 5 ms elapsed (1 ms in library) for CGo against near 454 ms elapsed (447 ms in library, one wazero build) for WASM. Warm: parse near 14 us, 3.3 KB, 70 allocations (CGo) against near 45 us, 85 KB, 78 allocations (WASM); scan near 2 us against 5 us. Harness binaries: CGo 13461954 bytes; WASM 20639362 bytes, 15403074 bytes when CGO_ENABLED=0. Pristine-cache builds: 6.7 s (CGo, clang mandatory) against 7.4 s (WASM, Go sufficient). Twelve hundred parse+scan pairs top out near 12 MB RSS (CGo) against near 300 MB passing RSS (WASM, 12 MB surviving forced collection).

Shipping context: distribution/build.go today compiles the launcher at CGO_ENABLED=0; plan.md tolerates Go/C source-build tooling selected alongside the SQL binding while end users stay toolchain-free. CGo is the maintainer-blessed pganalyze track with version tags (BSD-3-Clause plus PostgreSQL License); WASM is an independent track lacking tags (pseudo-version pin), MIT plus BSD NOTICE plus PostgreSQL-descended bytes plus Apache-2.0 wazero, dependent on WebAssembly threads with exception handling as wazero 1.12.0 implements them. canlc inspects SQL descriptors during transient batch executions.
common.purpose: Counsel Can solely on the proof enclosed below. Skip research, coding, and explanation. Wherever the proof leaves options tied, select the designated uncertainty result.

binding_choice.facts: Descriptor checks happen once per descriptor inside fleeting batch runs, tens of descriptors per project. CGo buys swift light canlc runs at the price of clang plus CGO_ENABLED=1 on all canlc build hosts, displacing the present CGO_ENABLED=0 launcher build. WASM buys toolchain-free canlc builds at the price of a per-process one-shot ~450 ms build with ~300 MB passing crest on SQL runs, a heavier binary, and a frozen untagged external hash. Trees, tokens, spans, and failure text/cursor pairs are the same either way.

error_vocabulary.facts: Failure reports on both tracks pair a message with Cursorpos, a character index into the statement, plus originating routine, file, line, and optional context. Manifest diagnostics for Can require byte windows into can.project.json statement bytes and a long-lived category for I37 to dispatch on without parsing upstream sentences. Sentences drift across libpg_query versions while cursor indexes stay put for identical input on an identical parser.

result_packaging.facts: Upstream parsing and scanning arrive through separate doors; each descriptor consumes statement inventory with extents from Parse and token inventory with extents from Scan. A merged adapter entry funnels both through one Go call into one structure; divided entries keep the passes callable apart for I37. Validation executes once per compile and never recurs at runtime.
